label: Typed knowledge graph
summary: Represent objects as stable vertices and relationships as named, directed edges. A graph stores assertions, not automatic truth.

label: Atomic concept and claim nodes
summary: Keep concepts, claims, formulas, sources, tasks, and artifacts distinguishable. Their identities must survive renaming.

label: Typed directed relations
summary: requires, supports, contradicts, derived_from, implements, and analogy have different semantics. Preserve direction and evidence.

label: Backlinks
summary: An incoming link is a reverse lookup of an existing edge, not a second independent source.

label: Unlinked mentions
summary: A matching name offers a link candidate. Resolve entity identity and meaning before treating it as a relation.

label: Entity identity and disambiguation
summary: Same label can denote different things; same object can have many labels. Stable IDs and explicit aliases reduce accidental merging.

label: Evidence provenance
summary: Keep source URL, exact version, date, section, access depth, and claim relationship separate from a summary.

label: Claim status and uncertainty
summary: Established theorem, approximation, measured result, preprint claim, disputed result, and open question must not share one undifferentiated confidence flag.

label: Content addressing
summary: Hash permitted source bytes or a canonical structured snapshot; a digest proves byte identity and does not prove truth.

label: Scope-first retrieval
summary: Select authorized observations before computing lexical statistics, graph propagation, and cache keys. The caller owns authentication.

label: Bitemporal evidence
summary: Separate when a fact applied from when it was recorded. Corrections append evidence rather than silently rewriting history.

label: Temporal validity intervals
summary: An observation is active when valid_from ≤ query_time < valid_until. Boundaries affect both graph edges and cached answers.

label: Immutable snapshots
summary: Write a content-addressed graph snapshot and then update its scope pointer. Keep original source identity with every derived artifact.

label: Event and decision ledger
summary: Record actual work, receipts, failures, owners, and next actions. An event is evidence of an operation, not a substitute for its artifact.

label: Write-ahead logs
summary: A transactional database can record changes before checkpointing state; its durability depends on the configured implementation.

label: SQLite transaction isolation
summary: Serialized writers and read snapshots are a possible next storage backend when filesystem snapshots become insufficient.

label: Result cache
summary: Reuse a derived result only when its query, snapshot, scope policy, algorithm, and time-dependent eligibility still match.

label: Memoization
summary: A cache is sound only when its key represents all output-relevant dependencies. Hidden mutable inputs break argument-only memoization.

label: Least recently used eviction
summary: Retain recently accessed entries subject to a capacity. Recency is a policy, not evidence quality or correctness.

label: Bounded FIFO eviction
summary: The supplied persistent result cache removes the oldest-written entries after 128 records. It is explicitly FIFO rather than LRU.

label: Time-to-live
summary: TTL limits reuse duration but cannot by itself detect a changed source or revoked scope. Version and validity checks are still required.

label: Dependency invalidation
summary: Include every semantically relevant dependency in the key, including source-only changes and policy versions.

label: Provider prompt cache
summary: Model-service prefix reuse is different from knowledge retrieval and local result caching; actual provider telemetry is required.

label: Attention key-value cache
summary: Cached intermediate key/value tensors reduce repeated attention computation during inference; they are not an editable evidence graph.

label: Tokenization
summary: Normalize text, choose word boundaries, handle domain symbols, and record stopword policy. These choices change ranking.

label: Inverse document frequency
summary: Rare query terms receive greater discriminating weight in a chosen eligible corpus. Compute counts after scope filtering.

label: BM25 lexical ranking
summary: Combine term saturation, document length normalization, and corpus frequency into an interpretable lexical baseline.

label: Embedding similarity
summary: A learned vector can place semantically similar passages near each other; closeness alone does not certify a claim or authorization.

label: Cosine similarity
summary: Compare vector directions after accounting for nonzero norms. Different embedding models create different geometries.

label: Adjacency matrix
summary: Matrix A encodes weighted vertex relations; its orientation convention must match transition equations.

label: Degree and hub effects
summary: A high-degree node can dominate navigation even when it is generic. Source references and analogy links need deliberate treatment.

label: Graph Laplacian
summary: L=D-A encodes local differences for an undirected nonnegative weighted graph. It has a constant-vector nullspace on each component.

label: Discrete Dirichlet energy
summary: The quadratic form sums weighted differences between linked vertices. Interpreting it as physical energy needs physical units and a calibrated model.

label: Grounding and boundary conditions
summary: Pin boundary values or impose a compatible gauge before inverting a singular Laplacian. Uniqueness depends on connectedness and boundary placement.

label: Heat diffusion on graphs
summary: Matrix exponentials smooth an initial signal according to graph connectivity. Smoothing can erase distinctions that evidence needs.

label: Random walk transition
summary: Normalize outgoing nonnegative weights. A vertex with no outgoing weight needs an explicit dangling-node rule.

label: Personalized PageRank
summary: Restart toward query seeds while traversing the eligible graph. The stationary mass is a retrieval affinity, not truth probability.

label: Contraction and convergence
summary: For restart probability above zero, the transition update contracts in L1. A reported iteration limit does not imply convergence.

label: Reciprocal rank fusion
summary: Combine lexical and graph rankings without pretending their raw scores have the same scale. Report the chosen constants.

label: Diversity-aware selection
summary: Balance query relevance against repetition; this is an optimization choice whose effects need a task benchmark.

label: Bounded evidence packets
summary: Limit the evidence sent to a model while preserving source locators and caveats. Track omitted items rather than silently implying full coverage.

label: Explanation paths
summary: Show why a node was retrieved and the typed relations linking it to direct matches. A path explains selection, not causation.

label: Bounded breadth-first traversal
summary: Visited identities and depth/node caps let cyclic knowledge graphs be explored without infinite traversal.

label: Prerequisite DAG
summary: A learning plan uses only prerequisite relations. General knowledge graphs may cycle even when the execution plan must not.

label: Cycle detection
summary: Kahn's algorithm reports a failed topological ordering; its remaining vertices can include descendants of cycles.

label: Idempotent operations
summary: Repeating the same snapshot ingest has no new state effect. A repeated external action still needs a provider-supported idempotency contract.

label: Durable checkpoints
summary: Save an artifact and its identity at a meaningful boundary. A claimed checkpoint without a readable artifact is incomplete.

label: Research improvement loops
summary: Each round changes a model or implementation in response to a specific observed weakness. Repeating a search is not automatically progress.

label: Stopping criteria
summary: Stop when acceptance is met, a bound is reached, or a decisive missing record blocks further progress; preserve the remaining question.

label: Retrieval baselines
summary: Compare lexical-only, graph-only, and fused retrieval on fixed questions and relevance labels before claiming a gain.

label: Recall and precision
summary: Count supported relevant evidence, not just generated answer fluency. Explicitly define the denominator and judging procedure.

label: Ranking quality
summary: Discount lower-ranked relevant items and normalize by an ideal order when relevance grades are well defined.

label: Abstention
summary: Return a gap when the available evidence cannot answer the question. A populated graph is not a reason to fabricate a match.

label: Temporal update tests
summary: Test future facts, expiry boundaries, corrections, and historical queries rather than only static fact lookup.

label: Calibration versus confidence
summary: A probability is calibrated only against outcomes with a defined evaluation population. Retrieval scores are not calibrated confidence.

label: Evaluation leakage
summary: Separate corpus preparation, answer labels, parameter tuning, and final evaluation. Duplicated sources are not independent confirmation.

label: Episodic memory
summary: In software, an episode can be an immutable observation or completed action; the biological notion involves richer behavioral and neural phenomena.

label: Semantic memory
summary: Curated concepts compress experience into reusable knowledge. Preserve links back to observations to detect errors introduced by compression.

label: Replay and consolidation
summary: Software can revisit cases and regression tests to consolidate a rule. This is a design analogy, not a demonstration of neural replay.

label: Hebbian associations
summary: Coactivation can strengthen a model connection, but cooccurrence alone is not evidence of cause, agreement, or truth.

label: Hopfield associative memory
summary: Under symmetric weights and asynchronous binary updates, a Lyapunov function can decrease toward stable states.

label: Attention-based association
summary: Attention mixes value vectors using query-key compatibility; particular modern Hopfield models establish a precise mathematical connection.

label: Forgetting and retention
summary: A decaying retrieval priority is a software policy. It must not delete durable evidence or imitate a universal human forgetting law.

label: Obsidian-compatible notes
summary: Export stable concept notes with typed link descriptions, sources, status, and formulas. Native links alone carry no theorem-verification status.

label: Foam in VS Code
summary: An editor-centered knowledge workflow can reuse portable Markdown notes and backlinks.

label: Logseq linked blocks
summary: Block-focused navigation provides another authoring granularity; retain explicit IDs during interchange.

label: Graphiti temporal graph
summary: A candidate external implementation for evolving relational memories, requiring its own deployment, licenses, and benchmark checks.

label: GraphRAG and global synthesis
summary: Community-level organization can help corpus-wide questions, but synthesis must remain auditable against original passages.

label: HippoRAG associative retrieval
summary: Personalized diffusion retrieves connected passages seeded by the question; the atlas uses a smaller deterministic graph baseline.

label: GraphRAG Zero
summary: A November 2026 provider research announcement describes retrieval built from embedding geometry with optional reasoning extensions.

label: Hindsight memory operations
summary: Study separation of retaining observations, recalling evidence, and reflecting; test each operation independently.

label: Mem0 consolidation
summary: Study selective memory extraction with revision and benchmark controls; product claims require exact configurations.

label: MemGPT memory tiers
summary: Treat active context as a scarce resource and durable evidence as an external store with explicit read/write operations.

label: Donna evidence handoff
summary: Give the assistant a bounded public evidence packet alongside separately authorized company knowledge. Do not infer a new access grant.

label: Skill memory workflow
summary: Before revisiting a problem, inspect relevant source-linked concepts, past decisions, unresolved objections, and versioned artifacts.

label: Repository knowledge graph
summary: Connect repo, commit, code path, test, source claim, and artifact with exact typed edges and distinct publication states.

label: Independent criticism
summary: A critic checks original evidence and assumptions, then identifies a concrete falsifier or repair. Agent agreement is not source independence.

label: Publication receipts
summary: A local commit, remote tree, workflow result, and live page are separate observations. Record each accurately.

label: Physics-to-memory operator bridges
summary: Laplacians, diffusion, oscillation, and energy functions can share mathematics while representing different physical or computational systems.

label: Spectral graph modes
summary: Eigenvectors form graph signal modes; eigenvalues become physical frequencies only after an explicit dynamical model and units.

label: Spin models and associative networks
summary: Some associative models resemble spin Hamiltonians mathematically; a software weight is not a measured magnetic coupling.

label: Association versus causation
summary: Graph adjacency is not a causal inference. Intervention, design assumptions, and competing explanations determine causal claims.

label: Lossy summary compression
summary: Summaries discard detail; preserve originals by pointer and maintain the ability to reopen source sections.

label: Information entropy
summary: Quantify uncertainty of a specified probability distribution. Entropy is not a substitute for epistemic quality or semantic understanding.

label: Cost and latency accounting
summary: Separate wall-clock time, local compute, provider tokens, and billable money. Report measured receipts, not inferred savings.

label: Question-led knowledge growth
summary: Store what would change the conclusion, prerequisites for answering it, and the next decisive source or experiment.
